metadata.notes: Dated authoritative cross-checks; some second publishers use original NWS or storm-report datasets. Editorial deferrals prevent same-story and same-hazard repeats. Zero publication approvals.

reviews.title_after: Rare snow and sleet dust southeast Alabama's Wiregrass region
reviews.core_fact: Snow and sleet reached southeast Alabama, southwest Georgia and part of the Florida Panhandle on January 17, 2018.
reviews.source_dependence: NWS Tallahassee retrospective and Alabama Weather Network's dated field meteorology report document the frozen precipitation; both refer to partly shared weather observations.
reviews.unverified_cautions: Separate Jan16 central-Alabama snow from Jan17 Wiregrass precipitation. Sleet amounts are not snow-depth measurements; avoid treating all regions as having the same accumulations.
reviews.graphic_concept: Original Gulf Coast arctic-air mass, precipitation-type and Wiregrass station map

reviews.title_after: A major snowstorm nearly matches Wichita's record
reviews.core_fact: A major winter storm blanketed Wichita on February 21, 2013; its 14.2-inch storm total was Wichita's second-highest single-storm total at the time.
reviews.source_dependence: NWS Wichita direct dated record and HPRCC regional monthly account document the Feb20–21 snow event; station-total observational lineage is shared.
reviews.unverified_cautions: 14.2 inches is a storm total, not a strict Feb21 midnight-to-midnight amount. Blizzard criteria differ by station; February22's other winter entry remains an adjacent-category concern.
reviews.graphic_concept: Original Wichita storm-total snow band and mesoscale frontogenesis diagram

reviews.title_after: A late-season nor'easter buries New Jersey roads in sleet
reviews.location_after: Gloucester County and Philadelphia suburbs, New Jersey
reviews.core_fact: A late-season nor'easter brought heavy sleet and snow to southern New Jersey and the Philadelphia suburbs on March 16, 2007.
reviews.source_dependence: NCEI Gloucester County storm segment and contemporaneous AccuWeather reporting corroborate the regional precipitation type/date, while the original local impact facts are NWS-derived.
reviews.unverified_cautions: Do not conflate sleet, freezing rain and snow or apply multiday March15–17 storm totals to March16 alone. This is one county segment of a larger storm.
reviews.graphic_concept: Original Gloucester County precipitation-type sounding and date-specific sleet/snow map

reviews.title_before: Thunderstorm Wind — District, District Of Columbia
reviews.title_after: An explosive derecho races across the Northern Plains
reviews.location_after: Eastern South Dakota and western Minnesota
reviews.core_fact: A fast-moving derecho brought destructive straight-line winds across eastern South Dakota and western Minnesota on May 12, 2022.
reviews.source_dependence: NWS Sioux Falls radar/impact archive and SDSU climatologist writeup corroborate date and region; their wind reports draw partly on the same NWS/SPC observation network.
reviews.unverified_cautions: Do not merge two convective lines or total tornado counts into a single track; measured 75+ mph counts and significant gust rankings require clear reporting-window definitions.
reviews.graphic_concept: Original hourly convective-line evolution, measured wind swath and dust plume map

reviews.title_before: Excessive Heat — TUCSON METRO AREA, Arizona
reviews.title_after: Wind-driven fires expand around Ruidoso as evacuations continue
reviews.location_after: Ruidoso and Mescalero Apache lands, New Mexico
reviews.core_fact: The South Fork and Salt fires continued spreading and forcing evacuations around Ruidoso on June 18, 2024, a day after their discovery.
reviews.source_dependence: NWS Albuquerque's 2024 fire-weather retrospective and Ruidoso's dated incident update separately corroborate June18 timing, but acreage and perimeters rely on shared incident reporting.
reviews.unverified_cautions: June17 was discovery/ignition reporting, June18 continued spread, June19 monsoonal rainfall; do not conflate. Fire-induced and synoptic winds are not interchangeable.
reviews.graphic_concept: Original June17–18 wind, humidity and incident-growth timeline

reviews.title_before: Excessive Heat — LAS VEGAS VALLEY, Nevada
reviews.title_after: Category 4 Hurricane Beryl strikes Carriacou, Grenada
reviews.core_fact: Hurricane Beryl made landfall on Carriacou, Grenada, at approximately 11:10 a.m. AST (15:10 UTC) July 1, 2024, as a Category 4 hurricane.
reviews.source_dependence: Contemporaneous NHC Tropical Cyclone Update determines local landfall timing and intensity; independent UN field reporting confirms Carriacou and July1, but refers to NHC intensity estimates.
reviews.unverified_cautions: Beryl became the earliest Atlantic Category 4 prior to this landfall, and reached Category 5 only later. Do not call it a Category 5 landfall or use later Caribbean loss totals as July1-only impact.
reviews.graphic_concept: Original Carriacou coastal map with local/UTC landfall fix and updated storm-track markers

reviews.title_after: Typhoon Doksuri's remnants leave Beijing under severe flooding
reviews.core_fact: Floodwaters and evacuations affected Beijing and Hebei on August 1, 2023, after days of extreme rain associated with Typhoon Doksuri's remnants.
reviews.source_dependence: WMO's Aug2 meteorological retrospective and AP's Aug1 reporting support event date/place via different channels; Chinese meteorological and response agencies supplied common rainfall/casualty source figures.
reviews.unverified_cautions: Extreme precipitation began days before August1. The reported 140-year station-record multi-day total must not be presented as a one-day Aug1 measurement; initial casualty reports were later updated.
reviews.graphic_concept: Original Doksuri remnant moisture-plume and July29–August1 rainfall/flood sequence

reviews.title_after: A damaging tornado tracks through Kasota and Mankato-area communities
reviews.location_after: Kasota, St. Peter and Mankato area, Minnesota
reviews.core_fact: A damaging tornado struck near Kasota and the Mankato area of south-central Minnesota on August 24, 2006.
reviews.source_dependence: NCEI original local tornado record and Minnesota DNR event history corroborate event/date; independent Minnesota Public Radio reporting covers the contemporaneous community impacts. Agency track data share NWS survey source.
reviews.unverified_cautions: Reported multiple touchdowns may represent one or several surveyed tornadoes; do not add their casualties/path lengths. Use historical F scale rather than EF for an August2006 tornado.
reviews.graphic_concept: Original surveyed Kasota/Mankato path and separate contemporary severe-weather reports

reviews.title_after: A severe geomagnetic storm carries brilliant auroras into October 11
reviews.location_after: North America and the British Isles
reviews.core_fact: Severe geomagnetic activity and auroral displays continued into October 11, 2024 across parts of North America and northern Europe.
reviews.source_dependence: NOAA NESDIS satellite imagery and British Geological Survey's separate magnetic observatory updates corroborate the Oct10–11 disturbance and auroral visibility from different instruments.
reviews.unverified_cautions: The CME arrived Oct10 EDT, and auroral photos may be dated Oct10 or Oct11 depending on UTC and local nighttime. G4 is a geomagnetic, NOT atmospheric wind or hurricane intensity classification; label as space weather.
reviews.graphic_concept: Original UTC/local geomagnetic timeline and latitude-binned auroral observations

editorial_deferrals.reason: May25 Parkersburg EF5 and May27 Jarrell F5 already occupy neighboring anniversary dates; avoid three successive tornado primaries.
October31 already has the same 1991 Perfect Storm; prevent consecutive duplicate storm stories.
Met Office dates Great Smog Dec5–9 and December5 already holds that primary; December4 was preceding stagnation, not core smog start.
September5 already has a separate California wildfire; avoid adjacent fire-weather stories until sequence revised.
